leafBlight.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
leafBlight.description: Bacterial leaf blight caused by Xanthomonas oryzae. Yellowing starts from leaf tips with wavy water-soaked margins and drying foliage.
leafBlight.immediate1: Drain standing water from the field for 3 to 4 days to reduce humidity.
leafBlight.immediate2: Avoid excess nitrogen top-dressing and overhead sprinkler irrigation.
leafBlight.immediate3: Remove and destroy severely infected leaves away from irrigation channels.
leafBlight.organic1: Spray 3% neem oil emulsion (30 ml per litre of water) every 7 days.
leafBlight.organic2: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens or Trichoderma viride at 5 grams per litre near the root zone.
leafBlight.organic3: Support plant immunity with potash or wood ash at 500 kg per hectare.
leafBlight.chemical1: Spray Copper oxychloride 50% WP at 2.5 to 3 grams per litre of water.
leafBlight.chemical2: Where advised by an agronomist, combine with agricultural bactericide at recommended dosage.
leafBlight.chemical3: Spray during dry morning or late afternoon hours only if over 25% foliage is affected.

powderyMildew.name: Powdery Mildew
powderyMildew.description: Fungal infection affecting shoots, flower panicles, and young nuts, leaving a white powdery coating on leaf surfaces.
powderyMildew.immediate1: Prune and safely destroy heavily affected shoots and dry panicles.
powderyMildew.immediate2: Improve airflow and sunlight penetration by selective canopy thinning.
powderyMildew.immediate3: Apply sprays early in the morning or evening to prevent leaf scorch.
powderyMildew.organic1: Spray wettable sulphur 80% WP at 2 grams per litre of water.
powderyMildew.organic2: Use 0.5% potassium bicarbonate or baking soda solution (5 grams per litre) on early spots.
powderyMildew.organic3: Follow up with neem-based botanical spray every 5 to 7 days.
powderyMildew.chemical1: Spray Hexaconazole 5% EC at 2 ml per litre of water.
powderyMildew.chemical2: Alternatively apply Propiconazole 25% EC at 1 ml per litre.
powderyMildew.chemical3: Alternate fungicide groups between sprays to prevent fungal resistance.
